name: Vance W. Amory International Airport
before:
Nevis has its own airport, on the north of the island just west of the village of Newcastle, in Saint James Windward Parish. The single runway is about 1,220 metres, which is short by international standards even though the airport carries international status.

The terminal, the control tower and the current runway length all date from the works completed in 2002, when the airport was renamed after Vance Amory, then Premier of Nevis.

Before that it was Newcastle Airport, and before that Bambooshay, so older references use all three names and it is worth checking which one a supplier is quoting against.
after:
Nevis has its own airport, at Newcastle on the north of the island. The single runway is about 1,220 metres.

It is named after Vance Amory. Newcastle Airport and Bambooshay Airport are earlier names, so older references use all three and it is worth checking which one a supplier is quoting against.

claims.note: The operator calls it the island's only airport; the government's fact page lists it as Nevis's airport.

claims.note: Was 'on the north of the island just west of the village of Newcastle'. Wikipedia places the airport at Newcastle (text and infobox); the operator, which runs the small port at Newcastle too, says Newcastle is on the northern side of the island; OurAirports keeps 'Newcastle Airport' as one of the airport's names. The exact position west of the village rests on Wikipedia alone, so it is dropped. The operator's site (naspakn.com) is where the address Wikipedia cites (nevisportsauthority.com) now leads.

Amory International Airport; the year and 'then Premier' rest on Wikipedia alone (cut below). As at St Kitts, no second source says in words that the airport is named after him; the name itself and Wikipedia's statement carry it.

claims.claim: just west of the village of Newcastle

claims.why: The position relative to the village rests on Wikipedia alone. Softened to 'at Newcastle on the north of the island' (see above).

Wikipedia, plus a Nevis Tourism Authority sentence ('located in Saint James Windward Parish, serves Nevis with a single 1,220-meter runway') that repeats Wikipedia's opening paragraph fact for fact, so it is not counted as independent. Of little use to an agent.

claims.claim: short by international standards despite international status
claims.wasBefore: which is short by international standards even though the airport carries international status
claims.why: A judgement, not a checkable fact. The runway length itself is kept.

claims.claim: terminal, control tower and runway length from works completed in 2002
claims.wasBefore: The terminal, the control tower and the current runway length all date from the works completed in 2002
claims.why: Wikipedia alone. The operator says only that there is 'a modern terminal building'; the Nevis Island Administration's pages had nothing on the works.

claims.claim: renamed in 2002 after Vance Amory, then Premier of Nevis
claims.wasBefore: when the airport was renamed after Vance Amory, then Premier of Nevis
claims.why: The year and 'then Premier' rest on Wikipedia alone (three tries: the operator's airport and about pages, and the Nevis Island Administration's Premier's Ministry page and home page). The naming is kept (see above).

claims.claim: the order of the old names
claims.wasBefore: Before that it was Newcastle Airport, and before that Bambooshay
claims.why: The order rests on Wikipedia alone; both names are kept without it (see above).

claims.claim: most travellers arrive via St Kitts and a short ferry
claims.why: Held back: replaces nothing in the old text, but matters to an agent. The Nevis Tourism Authority says regional, private and international connections arrive daily at Vance W. Amory, while most travellers arrive via St Kitts's Robert L. Bradshaw Airport and then take a short ferry. It could go in as an attributed statement.

quote: Regional flights, private jet services, and international connections arrive daily at Vance W. Amory International Airport (NEV), while most travellers choose to arrive via St. Kitts Robert L. Bradshaw Airport (SKB).
you're just a short ferry ride from Nevis' shores

sources.quote: short ferry rides across The Narrows from St. Kitts

claims.claim: scheduled flights: Cape Air, Winair, Trans Anguilla
claims.why: Held back: the old text names no airlines. The operator's live schedule lists Cape Air daily to St Thomas and St Croix, Winair weekly to St Maarten and Trans Anguilla daily to Anguilla, Antigua and St Eustatius. The two official sources disagree on Winair: the operator says weekly, the Nevis Tourism Authority advertises new daily Winair flights from St Maarten. Neither page is dated.
